calib.title: Colors aren't picked. They're calibrated.
calib.subtitle: Every shipped theme goes through the same pipeline: an explicit color contract, joint solving in perceptual space, per-item audits, and a sweep of the entire Forge input space.
calib.step.contract.title: Declare the contract
calib.step.contract.body: Each direction states its rules up front: minimum ΔE for critical pairs, allowed hue bands per signal lane.
calib.step.solve.title: Solve jointly
calib.step.solve.body: Neighboring roles are solved together for separation in perceptual color space; light variants also meet per-role contrast floors.
calib.step.audit.title: Gate on audits
calib.step.audit.body: Shipped themes are re-measured against the contract item by item — a failing audit blocks the commit.
calib.step.sweep.title: Sweep the input space
calib.step.sweep.body: The entire Forge input space is swept on a hue × saturation grid; every point must pass the same quality gates as the shipped themes.

surfaces.title: One color language, everywhere you work
surfaces.subtitle: There is exactly one semantic system: comments always recede, control flow always leans forward. Changing surfaces never changes meaning.
surfaces.vscode.title: Code editors
surfaces.vscode.body: Ember and Moss each ship dark and light builds for VS Code, Open VSX-compatible editors, and Zed, generated by the same audited pipeline.
surfaces.editorChannels.label: Code editor install channels
surfaces.obsidian.title: Obsidian
surfaces.obsidian.body: The Obsidian theme ships the Moss direction in dark and light, so notes and long-form reading use the same semantic system.
surfaces.obsidian.preview.title: Color as reading order
surfaces.obsidian.preview.copy: Quiet body text holds a steady rhythm; links, emphasis, and code step forward only when needed.
surfaces.web.title: This site itself
surfaces.web.body: Every color on this site derives from the theme tokens, and the body-text contrast budget is enforced by an audit on each commit — what you're reading is the calibrated output.
surfaces.web.preview.title: Every semantic has a place
surfaces.web.preview.copy: Body text stays steady while key actions move forward; one token set governs interface and code.
surfaces.availability.note: Ember and Moss ship for VS Code, VSX editors, and Zed; the Obsidian theme uses the Moss direction.
